details:
# **Preface**
As it stands, the current state of VRChat content on Oculus based hardware, as well as the compatibility of content between various PC builds, results in an inconsistent, sometimes infuriating, and even occasionally upsetting experience, for both users and developers.
Users will frequently find themselves in worlds which their headset or machine of choice cannot handle, experience everything from the slightest lag, to outright *machine failure*. Avatar compatibility is a mixed bag as well, with many avatars hidden behind "Avatar Rankings", which can be unreliable indicators *at best* of whether or not an avatar will be performant on their system.
Content creators also face dilemas in creating user content. On the Quest side, creators oft have to sacrifice key effects, due to harsh limitations on supported features, *or* may **completely avoid the platform altogether.** On PC, creators have no way of guaging whether their content will work on all systems, or just their own, resulting in a mish-mash of content which is inconsistently accessible to users. *In both cases **without a proper method of benchmarking content, creatros are left with the option to** (sometimes) **severely reduce the scope of their content, reduce the accessibility of their content, or completely abandon their content altogether out of either limitation or uncertainty**.
This provides a subpar experience for VRC users **and** creators who use *"consumer grade"* hardware for play and creation.
—
   
# **Proposal**
VRChat should provide content *benchmarking* functionality **within the VRChat user client**, with a *local content server* ( [related feedback ⇢](https://feedback.vrchat.com/quest-creators/p/provide-vrcsdk-localhost-quest-testing-server) ) ***provided by the VRCSDK***. Through content benchmarking, content can be more effectively ranked within the ecosystem, providing a safer, more robust user experience. Likewise, with content benchmarking, restrictions on mobile-oriented can **effectively be lifted** in exchange for required benchmarking. ( *See* [Mobile Benchmarking](#Mobile%20Benchmarking) *below* )
   
｜ **The Benchmark Server**
Building off of [Provide VRCSDK Local-host Quest Testing Server](https://feedback.vrchat.com/quest-creators/p/provide-vrcsdk-localhost-quest-testing-server), the VRCSDK will provide these new facilities:
- A specialized *VRChat content server*, located off of the machine's "*localhost*", accessible only to the local machine, and **over the Local Area Network** via the machines LAN address on a predetermined port.
- Internal software *to communicate with, and to automate interaction of, simulate additional users in, and collect metric data sent by, the VRChat client, as part of this server*.
- Support for *mobile-oriented* content.
This server utility, in function, would:
1. 'Spin Up' a VRChat content server session.
2. Prepare the project contents for testing (world or avatar).
3. Provide a button to "Send Invite Link" to the associated VRChat account linked to the SDK.
4. Await connection.
5. On successful connection of a VRChat *client*, serve project content.
6. Respond to commands and requests by *client* as necessary, as part of the benchmarking process, including *simulating additional users, simulating avatar behavior*, and *adjusting to feedback* by *client* request.
7. Retrieve *benchmark results* and terminate the session.
8. Assess results and give content the appropriate rating.
Content which then fails will not be permitted to upload. Content which passes below a reasonable threshold may be limited, either client-side as to where or how it can be used. ( *See* [Improved Ranking](#Improved%20Ranking) *below* )
   
| **Client Benchmarking**
The VRChat client will be updated with a "Developer Mode" toggle, which when enabled will enable access to locally-hosted content from an SDK connected to their account, as well as access to dedicated *Avatar Testing & Benchmarking tools*.
Upon connection to a *benchmarking session*, the *client* will place the user in the *benchmark world* (the **creator content**, in the case of worlds; the **avatar benchmarking space**, in case of avatars).
Once the benchmark has began, the *client* will first place the *user* in a predetermined *Benchmarking Dummy Avatar*, with *no components*, and *disable the user's locomotion and **non-hand** tracking*. Hand-tracking will remain enabled to allow suspension and cancellation of the benchmarking process.
> **Avatars**
In the case of avatars, an *Avatar Testing Bot*, a special form of simulated-user, will be spawned, across from the *user*, in the **avatar benchmarking space**. The client will then proceed to run through a series of tests within predetermined worlds:
- Display multiple *simulated users*, simulated by the *benchmarking server*, wearing predetermined avatars, which will proceed to animate, "speak", and move about the space.
- Run the *Avatar Testing Bot* through the *tested avatar* through the specified animations attached to the avatar, as well as testing toggles and other avatar effects, at multiple stages of *simulated user* saturation and world complexity.
- Record FPS and frame-drops during the testing period, noting the testing stage.
- Report back to the *benchmarking server*
> **Worlds**
In the case of worlds, the user will be spawned in the content being benchmarked. Similar to the avatar benchmarking, the client will run through a series of tests:
- Display multiple *simulated users*, simulated by the *benchmarking server*, wearing predetermined avatars, which will proceed to animate, "speak", and move about the space.
- Slowly move the user throughout the various spaces.
- Test the moving and spawning of interactive objects related to the world.
- Record FPS and frame-drops during the testing period, noting the testing stage.
- Report back to the *benchmarking server*
    
| **Improved Ranking**
In place of the current *Avatar Performance Rankings*, and new **Content Performance Ranking** system will be created. This system will be split into two forms of ranking:
- **Perfomance**: The ranking provided by the benchmarking utility.
- **Estimated Performance**: The rank of the avatar or world based on VRChat recommended upload specifications, similar to the old *Avatar Performance Ranking system*.
If content has been benchmarked, it will display the **Performance Ranking**. Otherwise, content will display the **Estimated Performance** in its place.
Likewise, the **Performance** ranking will have the additional ranks of *Incompatible* & *Degraded*. Any content which is given the *Incompatible* rating is content which has **failed** benchmarking, and shall be barred from upload until a successful pass has been recorded.
- For avatars, this would optimally be *any avatar that fails to run at an average of 60FPS, with a floor of 45FPS, in an open space with no users*.
- For worlds, this would optimally be any world that runs less than 60FPS average, with a floor of 45fps, with 10 or less users.
Content which is ranked as *Degraded* will be **specific to avatars**, and is described as content which will definitively have a greater effect on the stability of other users in VRChat. This content **will be *blocked* regardless of safety settings**, and *will require the user to **manually show these avatars, per user***. This differentiates itself from "*Very Poor*", which is content that *may* degrade performance in most cases.
Benchmarked worlds will also have an additional **Capacity** rating. This rating will provide the suggested *maximum capacity* of the world for optimal performance (peak benchmark recorded FPS) with good-ranked avatars. This will allow users to make educated decisions when hosting events in VRChat space, and give better idea as to whether a world is worth visiting with their current party. Hosts may optionally enforce the capacity rating to prevent instances from exceeding it for maximum performance.
Content will still be allowed to upload against VRC recommendations, which are adjusted as necessary, using the **Estimated Performance** ranking, *without benchmarking*, permitting it falls within current limitations.
PC **Performance** ratings will be *weighted* based on the hardware specifications of the user, compared to the Recommended Specifications of the PC client. E.G. Systems falling below the recommended specifications will receive *X increase to its internal score, whereas systems falling above the recommended specifications will receive X% decrease to its internal score.
    
| **Mobile Benchmarking**
For mobile content creation (e.g. Quest), the following changes will be made as follows:
- Previously "disallowed" content, which was permitted for PC, but restricted or removed from Quest, will be changed to "conditional", requiring a passing (non-*Incompatible* or *Degraded*) ranking in order to be uploaded to VRC. (e.g. material shaders, post-processing)
- Content falling within the traditional VRC Quest Content Limitations may bypass benchmarking, and will be ranked against the **Estimated Performance** ranking.
- Benchmarking will be carried out client-side, identically to PC, as described above. – Any Quest unit connected to the same local area network as the development machine, permitting optimal network conditions (firewall, port monitoring), will be able to connect to the development machine's *benchmarking server* with the same VRC account as the SDK.
—
    
# **Summary**
Through these proposed, or similar, changes, these benefits may be found:
1. Content previously restricted or removed due to performance and abuse concerns will instead be **conditionally allowed** based on its performance ranking. **This will give creators greater freedom in creating cross-platform content.**
2. Content previously allowed on estimated metrics, *which in practice do not work on mobile hardware, or the recommended hardware in the case of PC*, can be stopped before upload. **This gives users a safer, more consistent experience across the VRChat ecosystem.**
3. Content previously unfairly ranked based on estimated metrics, *which in practice have little additional overhead in normal use cases*, will be given more accurate performance rankings, which **will also aid in giving users a safer, more consistent experience across the VRChat ecosystem.**
title: Proposal for VRChat SDK Creator Benchmarking Functionality
